text:
maria: heads up — seeing steady memory creep on streaming tool-loop sessions (~30-60m). KV cache active_pages keeps growing even after eviction ticks. attaching quick heap summary.

aj: can you paste the kv stats?

maria: quick dump: ```kv.active_pages=134112
kv.free_pages=8120
kv.pinned_pages=3124
kv.age_bucket[0]=20128
kv.age_bucket[1]=50200
kv.age_bucket[2]=59864
eviction_ticks=120
evict_threshold=0.6```

kevin: yikes, age_bucket[2] that high suggests pages are drifting into old buckets and not being reclaimed. eviction policy looks conservative for sustained long contexts. also: which kernel path are these requests hitting — fused fastpath or generic lookup?

maria: profiler (samples over 60s window) shows ~12% in `fastpath::fused_kv_lookup` vs ~0.5% historically. hypothesizing the kernel selector now prefers fused path for long seqs which may be holding onto page refs.

tash: repro steps? I can run locally.

maria: repro: spin up streaming chat + toolloop that emits calls every 2s, sequence length grows with inputs. run ~45m. quick command: `./scripts/run_e2e.sh --mode=stream --toolloop --seq=4096 --clients=5 --duration=45m`

aj: tried a lightweight repro on A100 with quantized runtime — same drift. on CPU-run didn't reproduce. allocator counters: ```alloc.pages_in_use=134112
slab_frag_ratio=0.16
page_ref_leaks_detected=0 (but that counter only increments on explicit refcount asserts)```

kevin: plausible root cause: fastpath caches a pointer to page frames for micro-ops and forgot to clear/decrement when a batch exits early (toolloop early-return case). that keeps a soft hold and prevents eviction, plus pages age into older buckets.

maria: i tried a quick local patch adding a `release_page_ref()` in `fastpath::exit_hot_path()` — after that two 1-hour runs show stabilised page counts (active_pages ~= 84k steady). i'll open a PR for proper fix.

infra-bot: deploy-preview created: PR #4821 — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 :eyes:

tash: nice. can we also try lowering `kv.evict_age_threshold` from 0.6 -> 0.3 and run canary to see if policy changes mitigate until fix lands?

maria: scheduling a canary on `dedicated-6a` cluster with the patch + evict threshold tweak. i'll post heap diffs once done.

aj: small note — batching heuristics may compound this: continuous batching keeps prefix cache entries live across many micro-batches. try `batch.max_window_ms=5` to reduce cross-batch residency in the canary.

kevin: agreed. if patch is small let's canary quickly. if stable, roll to beta runtime. also add a unit test around early-exit in fastpath to catch regressions.

maria: thanks — will follow up with logs and heapdiffs. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.``
